title: PRD for 10-min city rebalancing
persona: Kabir, senior PM at Blinkit on logistics
scenario: Blinkit promises 10-minute delivery in 30 cities. In 4 of them, P95 delivery time has crept past 14 minutes because the dark-store mix is wrong, too many fast-movers in some, too few in others. Eng wants a PRD to build a weekly auto-rebalancing engine. You have the metrics, the constraints, and a strong opinion. You don't have an obvious template, every PRD in this org reads differently.
badPrompt: write a PRD for SKU rebalancing
badOutput:
Product Requirements Document

Objective: Optimize SKU distribution across dark stores.
Features: Auto-rebalancing, demand forecasting, alerts.
Success metrics: Faster delivery, less waste.
Timeline: TBD.
Owners: TBD.

hints.title: Define the PRD sections you want
hints.body: List the sections: problem, non-goals, user stories, success metrics, edge cases, open questions. Without this, Claude gives you a generic template.

hints.title: Anchor decisions, not just requirements
hints.body: Demand a ‘key decisions’ section with options + chosen path + rejected paths. PRDs without this read like wish-lists.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a PRD, not a vague write-up.
Name the problem, SKU rebalancing across dark stores.
Anchor the metric, P95 delivery time creeping past 14 minutes.
Specify the scope, 4 of 30 cities. Concentrated, not systemic.
Lock the cadence, weekly auto-rebalance, not real-time.
Add non-goals. Without them, scope creeps in the first review.
Reference the audience, eng team building this. PRD format calibrates to readers.
Ask for a decisions section with options + rejected paths.
Define the PRD sections explicitly, problem, user stories, metrics, edge cases, open questions.
Specify the output structure, markdown sections, not prose.

tipIfLow: PRDs from AI are generic by default. The fix is to define the sections AND demand a decisions section with rejected paths. The unlock isn't ‘write a PRD’, it's ‘write the parts of a PRD that force me to commit to choices’.
goldPrompt: Act as a senior PM at Blinkit. I'm Kabir, logistics PM. P95 delivery time has crept past 14 minutes in 4 of 30 cities because dark-store SKU mix is wrong. Eng wants a PRD for a weekly auto-rebalancing engine. Write the PRD in markdown with these exact sections: Problem (with numbers), Non-goals, User stories (driver, store-ops, demand-planner), Success metrics with thresholds, Edge cases, Open questions, AND a 'Key decisions' section listing options + chosen path + 2 rejected paths with reasons. Ban vague 'TBD' fields. Audience: eng team building this in Q2.
